questions.question: In the Kojiki's cosmogony, what produces the first island, Onogoro?
options: A. Amaterasu commands the earth to rise out of the ocean
B. Izanagi and Izanami stir the brine with the Heavenly Jewel Spear; the drops that fall from the tip harden into an island
C. A primordial giant's body is divided into the islands of Japan
D. The underworld pushes upward and breaks through the surface of the ocean
questions.explanation: The creation act in the Kojiki is explicitly artisanal: Izanagi and Izanami stir the brine with the Heavenly Jewel Spear from the Floating Bridge of Heaven, and the dripping brine solidifies into Onogoro. This is creation by craft, not command.

questions.question: Izanagi's three greatest children — Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo — are born when he:
options: A. Cuts apart the fire god Kagutchi with his sword
B. Descends to Yomi and returns carrying Izanami's spirit
C. Washes his face in a river after returning from the underworld
D. Receives the jeweled spear from the Separate Heavenly Deities
questions.explanation: The Three Precious Children (mihashira no uzu no mikoto) are born from Izanagi's ritual purification (misogi) after he returns from Yomi. Amaterasu comes from washing his left eye, Tsukuyomi from his right eye, and Susanoo from his nose. This links the supreme sun goddess's origin to the act of cleansing from death's pollution.

questions.question: The Kojiki's structure of seven divine generations before the active creation by Izanagi and Izanami serves primarily a decorative purpose, filling pages before the real narrative begins.
questions.explanation: The divine procession is structurally meaningful, not decorative. It establishes that the universe is organized genealogically from its first moment — the same form (X begat Y) that governs the human imperial sections of the text appears at the origin of time. It also creates a deliberate countdown, making Izanagi and Izanami's creative act feel like the culmination of a prepared sequence.

questions.question: Why does the Kojiki explain the Leech-Child's malformation by saying Izanami spoke first in the marriage ritual? What is this kind of narrative doing?
questions.sample_answer: The narrative is using the creation story to legitimate a specific ritual practice — that the male should speak first in the marriage ceremony. By embedding the norm in a cosmic creation story, the text makes it more than a rule: it becomes the way things were done when the world itself was first made correctly. Getting it wrong produced a malformed result; getting it right produced Japan. This pattern — myth explaining and grounding social or ritual norms — is characteristic of how mythological texts function across cultures.
key_concepts: consequence of error as explanation of rule

questions.question: After Izanagi and Izanami separate at the entrance to Yomi, they make statements through the boulder. Izanami says she will kill a thousand people per day; Izanagi says he will cause fifteen hundred births. What is this exchange explaining?
options: A. Why Izanami became a goddess of death
B. The origin of the fixed relationship between the rate of death and the rate of birth in the human world
C. Why Izanagi chose not to return to the underworld again
D. The reason that Amaterasu rules heaven rather than the underworld
questions.explanation: The exchange at the boulder is an etiology — a story explaining the origin of a natural fact. The rates of death and birth in the world are here given a divine origin: Izanami's promise to kill thousands, balanced against Izanagi's counter-promise to create even more. Population growth is encoded in the founding cosmic agreement between the first divine couple.
